tags.gist: Calls the competency-based approach the right frame but says it lacks credentialing's measurement properties, which must be re-established for a stochastic examinee.
Wants competency evaluation to complement software validation, with every competency claim scoped to a task, population, oversight level and version.
Proposes a new element testing whether clinical judgment stays unaffected by account history, persistent memory, personalization and what the user asserts or claims.
Wants clinicians to prespecify a taxonomy separating perturbations which must leave the output unchanged from those which must change it.
Wants every gating benchmark to carry a validity argument on the five standard sources of validity evidence, including links to clinical-confirmation outcomes.
Prefers sequestered, independently governed item banks; a sponsor benchmark may gate only if prespecified, custodian-held and independently scored.
Treats the case, not the run, as the unit of inference, reporting variance components and applying zero-failure bounds to safety-critical behavior.
Treats the clinician panel as a measuring instrument with reported reliability, and wants safety elements held to conjunctive standards proficiency cannot offset.
Would make clinician-device team performance the primary criterion whenever a clinician takes part in the decision, counting how often incorrect outputs are adopted.
Wants image-ablation and image-substitution tests for vision-language devices, with cases where color-coded classifications diverge from the correct reading.
Presumes each new foundation-model version is a different examinee, scaling re-examination to observed behavioral change rather than the update's nominal size.
Supports the competency approach: where inputs and outputs cannot all be enumerated, competence must be inferred from a performance sample, as for clinicians.
Says the case for the approach rests on the output's form, an open-ended recommendation without a single reference label, not on whether models reason.
Keeps cybersecurity, version control, logging and failure-mode analysis as necessary but insufficient, since none shows clinical competence.
Says the analogy carries credentialing's structure but not its psychometric properties, such as case numbers, examiner reliability and standards, which must be rebuilt.
Notes a device, unlike a person, can be re-tested on one case under counterfactual variation, provided memory and personalization settings are fixed and disclosed.
Wants competency claims scoped like entrustment, to version, configuration, task, population and oversight level, with new evidence to move along the activity axis.
Shares the cited concern that accountability is where the analogy weakens; the credentialable thing is the socio-technical system with responsibility allocated explicitly.
Says the robustness element misses state persisting across sessions and deference to user assertions, which bend judgment toward the user.
Cites own work on cross-session adaptation and wants evaluation to test the conditioned state that memory and personalization produce, especially on ambiguous inputs.
Cites sycophancy findings and says the elements cover symptom minimizing and emotional manipulation, yet omit pressure from an expert user.
Wants both capitulation under disagreement and rigidity toward new evidence tested, as appropriate corrigibility: updating on evidence, not assertion.
Says repeated runs cannot catch this directional error; it needs paired counterfactual presentations with and without conditioned history and user belief.
Recommends an element on invariance to user state and belief, covering history, memory, personalization and expert assertion, scored in both directions.
Wants invariance specified in both directions: paraphrase and history must not change output, while a risk-changing finding or patient sex must.
Points to metamorphic testing, which checks prespecified relations between related inputs, with a glaucoma example of invariance and directional relations.
Recommends sponsors prespecify with clinicians, before testing, a perturbation taxonomy listing both invariance and directional relations.
Treats a gating benchmark as a high-stakes test and wants a validity argument along the five sources in the educational testing standards.
Says an item validated on human examinees must be re-validated for a model whose jagged capability profile fails easy items and passes hard ones.
Cites a study where models alone found the condition far more often than lay users with the same models, which standard benchmarks did not predict.
Wants the validity argument to include a content blueprint mapping items to intended-use tasks, with coverage by condition, severity and population.
Wants rubric and adjudicator reliability plus behavioral evidence from perturbation, ablation and counterfactual tests, not the model's stated rationale.
Wants the benchmark's internal structure examined, reporting subscores only when reliable.
Wants benchmark scores correlated with clinical-confirmation results on the same device, as proof that benchmark results predict behavior in practice.
Wants the classes of error a benchmark cannot detect stated explicitly.
Recommends sequestered banks under independent third-party custody, sponsor benchmarks only with custodian-held items and independent scoring, and specialty consortia maintaining banks.
Makes the case the unit of inference: intervals computed at case level by mixed-effects models or clustered bootstrap, not pooled runs.
Wants variance components across case, run, paraphrase, context and adjudicator reported, with decision studies setting how many of each are needed.
Says results are intervals, wide with few cases; comparisons need paired designs over shared cases, and rankings need uncertainty on the ranks.
Applies zero-failure bounds: bounding a safety-critical failure rate below one percent needs about three hundred independent failure-free cases.
Applies the same arithmetic inside a case: a handful of identical runs still permits a sizeable per-run deviation probability.
Recommends deriving the numbers of cases and runs from the required precision, reporting both levels and the bound each zero-failure count supports.
Treats the panel as an instrument: report inter-rater agreement and rater numbers, and grade open-ended outputs against a set of acceptable answers.
Says the median clinician must be sampled with uncertainty; suggests standard of care for safety, the realistic alternative for benefit, specialist standards for specialist questions.
Wants thresholds from established standard-setting methods, with conjunctive standards: failing a safety element is not compensated by proficiency elsewhere.
Wants an LLM adjudicator's agreement with the human panel shown on a held-out sample, and from a different model family than the device.
Makes clinician-device team performance the primary criterion when a clinician decides, with device-alone secondary, and reports an error-propagation rate.
Says the approach fits vision-language devices, but their benchmarking needs two added tests and a wider perturbation taxonomy.
Wants image-ablation and image-substitution tests on cases where the image carries the decisive finding, to show the image drives the answer.
Wants benchmark cases where normative color codes in imaging reports diverge from the correct interpretation, so devices cannot shortcut via flags.
Wants the perturbation taxonomy to cover acquisition device, protocol, image quality, overlays and accompanying text, oversampling ambiguous images.
Treats each upstream foundation-model version as presumptively a new examinee, with re-examination depth scaled to observed behavioral change.
Proposes three re-examination tiers: sentinel testing on every change, targeted re-benchmarking of sensitive elements, and full re-examination when material change appears.
Wants evaluation version-pinned and provider contracts guaranteeing pinned-version access and deprecation notice long enough to finish re-examination.
Wants re-examination on statistically linked forms from a sequestered bank, so score changes reflect the device rather than test optimization.
Proposes a sentinel set of safety-critical cases run on a schedule against the deployed configuration, catching silent updates; changed outputs trigger review.
Closes: evaluate the device as a competence, examined as a distribution, tested for user-conditioned drift and certified in scope by independent examiners.
